payload.analysis: The retrieved HRM reveals absent esophageal peristalsis, elevated IRP, and impaired LES relaxation, which are diagnostic of achalasia rather than refractory GERD. Normal endoscopy and biopsies exclude eosinophilic esophagitis and mucosal injury, while PPI failure and solid-food dysphagia are fully explained by this motility disorder. The leading hypothesis of refractory GERD is thus refuted, and achalasia becomes the most credible diagnosis. All key diagnostic information has been covered.

payload.report: The patient's chronic PPI-refractory heartburn, regurgitation, and solid-food dysphagia are explained by a motility disorder rather than refractory GERD. HRM shows absent peristalsis, elevated IRP, impaired LES relaxation, and increased intraesophageal pressure, meeting achalasia criteria. Normal endoscopy and negative biopsies exclude eosinophilic esophagitis and malignancy. Pathologist and radiologist analyses confirm achalasia; panesophageal pressurization supports type II subtype. Thus the patient has type II achalasia.
